core_obligations: Reformulate (proof lines 3027-3028): by the cited same-chapter lemma, for a K-flat complex the functor Tot(- tensor K^bullet) is exact on the derived category, hence preserves acyclicity.

Characterise quasi-isomorphisms by cones (proof lines 3028-3030): a morphism of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its cone is acyclic, and the functor commutes with the formation of cones.
Conclude (proof line 3030): applying the functor to a quasi-isomorphism produces a morphism whose cone is again acyclic, so the image is a quasi-isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Turn K-flatness of K^bullet into exactness of the tensor product functor with it.
Recall that quasi-isomorphisms are exactly the morphisms with acyclic cones.
Since the functor is exact it carries acyclic cones to acyclic cones.
Hence it carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms (statement lines 3010-3024). The proof is a two-input reduction: the cited same-chapter lemma turns K-flatness into exactness of the functor Tot(- tensor K^bullet), and the characterisation of quasi-isomorphisms by acyclicity of their cones turns exactness into preservation of quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 3027-3030). The content is the pair of standard facts and the observation that the functor is compatible with cones. The claim is H2: one reduction, with both inputs named.
